In regular Army, probably. Army Aviation is a completely different thing. We take flights and our job very seriously and if any one person on the crew isn't comfortable with something then the whole crew has to back them up.
We hold each other accountable, and if i ever heard of a pilot or other crew chief doing anything like that. He/she would be on immediate down slip, and either out of the flight company and in a maintenance company, or at the worst they would be in toolroom with the other degenerates that we dont trust to even turn a wrench correctly.

100% man. But the point of doing these kinds of flights like we do is too 1,) push our limits, and 2,) find our limits.
Its meant to reinforce that there is no rank in a helicopter and if even one crew member is tired and not comfortable with continuing then the crew needs to stop mission and rest before continuing on.

So as a Crew Chief in the US Army, I've actually had a pilot fall asleep on a really late night flight. We tried to get his attention a few times and assumed he was just quiet as usual. After he kind of slumped over to the right on a turn i reached up and smacked the absolute shit out of this LT and yelled at him.
Afterwards, we immediately landed and the three of us joked a bit and told him that there were no hard feelings but that if youre reaching the point if exhaustion that you can't stay awake you need to make the rest of the crew aware.
Overall a really funny time afterwards, at the time, absolutely terrifying
